docstring: A cheap rung of a fidelity ladder may be used to SCREEN only after its rank agreement with the rung that decides has been measured on this design, and the agreement must be published beside any ranking derived from it. Correlation of magnitude is not agreement of order, and order is the only thing a screen uses. Where the agreement has not been measured, the ladder may still run every candidate to the deciding rung — that costs budget, which is visible — but it may not prune, which costs the answer and is not.
fix_action: Require, before any rung below the deciding one is allowed to eliminate a candidate, a measured rank agreement between that rung and the deciding rung over a set of candidates carried to both. Publish the agreement with the ranking and refuse to prune when it is absent, falling back to carrying every candidate. The plugin already ships this idea for another track, where a bench measurement must be shown to correlate with its simulated prediction before the prediction is trusted — use it as the reference implementation rather than inventing one. MEASURED, and it is an ORDER INVERSION rather than a loose fit: over the rewrite candidates the cheap rung reports minus 21.3, minus 6.7 and minus 2.6 percent, and the deciding rung reports minus 3.3, minus 4.3 and minus 1.3 for the same three. The candidate that wins by a factor of three on the cheap rung places THIRD on the deciding one, and the true winner is second-best on the cheap rung. A screen keeping the cheap top candidate discards the answer. The cause is physical and general: the cheap rung cannot see that the winning candidate was buying away a structure the later stage charges for, measured here as plus 580 square micrometres of added buffering against 628 saved by the removed registers. SWEPT, and the sweep is a warning about WHERE to read, without which the check would be born vacuous. The cheap rung has a designated per-trial artefact, and across the published corpus it is present 21 times and EMPTY 21 times -- the rung emitted nothing, anywhere. A check keyed on that artefact therefore opens 21 files, finds no candidate ranking in any of them, has nothing to compare, and reports success: an empty population passing as a clean one, which is the failure this batch documents against other people's guards and found once in its own verifier. The evidence for the inversion is real and lives somewhere else -- in the cross-layer lane's own analysis, which states that a pre-PnR area model would have ranked these arms in a different order and that the lane can measure which order is right, and gives the mechanism: the flow charges for a carry chain at a rate synthesis does not show. BUILD IT FROM THE TWO RANKINGS THAT EXIST -- the order the cheap model predicts and the order the measured results give -- and make the emptiness itself a refusal: a rung that ranked nothing has not earned agreement, and must not be reported as agreeing.

design: the flow declaration and its consumers; no design involved
rule_name: a consumer must resolve a declared output path rather than guess among candidates
pattern: A step writes an artefact wherever its own option points. A later consumer needs that artefact and locates it by trying an ordered list of names it carries in its own source, taking the first that exists. The flow document ALREADY declares the path, and the consumer never reads it — so one artefact has two definitions of where it lives, and the list is where they drift. Nothing detects the drift, because a consumer that finds nothing reports the artefact as absent, which is indistinguishable from a step that did not run.
docstring: Where the flow declares a step's output path, that declaration is the single definition of where the artefact lives, and a consumer must resolve it from there. A private candidate list re-implements the same fact in a second place, and the failure it produces is silent in the worst direction: the artefact is reported absent rather than mislocated, so the axis it feeds degrades to not-measured and the run stays green. A list remains legitimate where the flow declares nothing, and as a fallback BEHIND the declaration — but then the fallback must be disclosed when it fires, because a consumer that quietly found the file under its second-choice name has evidence the declaration is wrong.
fix_action: Resolve every declared artefact through the flow declaration; keep a candidate list only as a disclosed fallback, and report which name satisfied the lookup so a second-choice hit is visible rather than silent. Refuse a candidate list whose first entry contradicts the declaration. MEASURED on this tree: 48 consumers carry an ordered candidate-path list for a single artefact; 33 of those name at least one path the flow document ALREADY declares; and of those 33, only 3 are in a program that reads the flow declaration at all — the other 30 guess. The instance that surfaced this is a reliability screen whose consumer tries three names, one of which the flow does not know about, so the axis is reachable only by a coincidence of naming. Some of the 30 may be supporting older trees deliberately, which is why the rule orders the declaration first rather than deleting the lists.

design: the layer's command-line contract; no design involved
rule_name: which stream carries the summary is part of the contract and must be driven to a real verdict
pattern: An interface fixes which output stream carries the human summary and which carries a refusal, so that a caller can capture one without the other and a grep over a log means something. Nothing enforces it, because the obvious test — run the command and look — is run with no arguments, which produces an argument-parser error rather than a verdict. So every program looks identical under the test, the clause is never measured, and programs drift onto whichever stream their author reached for.
docstring: Stream assignment is part of a command's contract, not a formatting preference: a caller that captures one stream and not the other gets a different answer depending on which program it invoked, and a log grep that finds nothing cannot distinguish a clean run from a summary written where nobody looked. Enforcing it requires driving each command to a REAL verdict, because the argument-parser error path is on the refusal stream for every command and tells you nothing about the clause.
fix_action: Give each command a known-verdict invocation in the layer's own contract test — an input that produces a finding, and one that produces a could-not-check — and assert per stream that the summary lands where the interface says and the refusal marker lands on the other. MEASURED, two-sided, on comparable runs: the comparison command driven to a vacuous corpus puts its summary line on the output stream and its could-not-check marker on the error stream, which is the contract observed exactly; the contract command driven to a real document with sixteen findings puts EVERYTHING on the error stream, summary line included, leaving the output stream empty. One conformant, one not, out of the two I drove to a real verdict — the other seventeen are NOT MEASURED and are not claimed. THE SCREEN WARNING, EARNED: running each command with no arguments and comparing stream byte counts reports eighteen of nineteen on the error stream and is worthless, because that is the argument-parser path. It measures argparse, not the contract. THE NUMBERS, because this record described its measurement in words and carried no figure, and the implementing lane needs the figure rather than the narrative: the layer presents 19 commands. Exactly 2 were driven to a real verdict -- one conformant, one not -- and the remaining 17 are NOT measured and are not claimed, because driving each needs valid inputs per command. Do not substitute a no-argument invocation for that work: an earlier probe did, compared stream byte counts, and reported 18 of 19 'on stderr', which measures the argument parser rather than the contract.

design: the plugin's own test tree; no design involved
rule_name: a third-party import at test module scope must be guarded or it aborts collection
pattern: A test file imports an optional third-party package at module scope. On a host without it the import fails during COLLECTION, before any test function exists — so the file contributes no pass, no fail and no skip, and a roll-up that counts those three sees nothing missing. Worse, the collection error interrupts the whole session rather than that one file, so a single unguarded import in a tree of hundreds turns a full run into no run. The same dependency is usually handled correctly on the product side, where a guard degrades it to a stated could-not-check, which is what makes the test-side omission easy to miss: the codebase demonstrably knows how.
docstring: An optional dependency imported at test module scope must be guarded so the file yields a declared NOT-RUN rather than a collection error. The distinction is not cosmetic: a skip is a result and appears in the roll-up, while a collection error is the absence of results and interrupts the session, so the run reports nothing rather than reporting less. Route the guard through whatever tier the suite uses for infrastructure-shaped non-runs, because a bare skip is the same omission one level up — invisible to the count that is supposed to notice it.
fix_action: Walk every test module's top-level imports; for each name that resolves to neither the standard library nor anything in the repository, require the import to sit inside a guard that yields a declared not-run carrying the remedy. MEASURED: 51 test files import one third-party package at module scope with no guard, and it is exactly ONE package — no other third-party dependency in the whole test tree is imported unguarded, so the fix is bounded and mechanical. PROVEN, with a positive control on the same blocked dependency: the test file reports `1 error during collection` and `Interrupted`, running ZERO tests and stopping the session, while a program consuming the same package degrades to a stated could-not-check with a non-zero code. The originating lane found two of the 51 and judged them latent because the host had the package; the count is what makes it worth doing. BEWARE THE SCREEN: a name is only third-party if it resolves nowhere in the repository — matching against a list of module stems misclassifies in-repo packages and reports 216. RE-RUN on the merged tree with the screen stated above: 50 occurrences across 50 files, still exactly ONE package, so the fix stays bounded and mechanical. Main touched six test files and none is in the set. Two things the re-run settled that the original did not say out loud: the test runner must be excluded from the population, because a run without it does not reach collection at all and counting it inflates the figure roughly thirtyfold; and the in-repo name set must include DIRECTORY names, not only module stems -- dropping that term reported 174 files instead of 50, reproducing the documented over-match while re-measuring the record that documents it.

design: the capture loop itself; no design involved
rule_name: a distilled rule must be routed into a program some verdict consults
pattern: The whole purpose of turning a recovery into a deterministic rule is that the next run recovers it with no agent present. That holds only if something invokes the program the rule lands in. Routing is chosen by naming the program that OWNS the subject, which is the right criterion for correctness and says nothing about whether anything runs it — and the tree separately tracks gates that no automatic verdict consults. Nothing joins the two, so a capture can be perfectly routed, perfectly implemented, and silent forever, while the record and the routing table both read as complete.
docstring: Routing a rule to the program that owns its subject is necessary and not sufficient: the program must also be one that something invokes. A rule in a program no verdict consults is indistinguishable, from every artefact the capture produces, from a rule that fires and finds nothing — and it is worse than an unwritten rule, because the record asserts the class is now covered. Join the routing table to the wiring census at emit time and refuse the pairing, rather than discovering it when a later run does not catch the thing the record promised.
fix_action: At emit time, resolve each record's target program through the routing table and check it against the wiring census the tree already maintains — the one that lists gates no automatic verdict consults, together with its standing baseline. Refuse a record whose target is unwired, naming both the record and the program, and say which of the two must change: wire the program, or route the rule to one that runs. MEASURED on this batch, and RE-MEASURED after it grew: 26 Bucket-A records resolve to 16 distinct programs and NONE of them is unwired (it was 21 into 15 when the rule was written; re-running the check is the rule applying to itself), so the batch passes the check it is proposing — which is the result to want and not the one to assume, because I did not verify it until I wrote this rule. The census on this tree reports 619 gates with 61 unwired against a baseline of 59, and names three as newly unwired; one of those three is a program of the very layer this batch is about, so the pairing was reachable rather than hypothetical. TWO SELF-INSTANCES, both found in this batch's own verifier and both of the shape 'the artefact is present and the thing that should consume it consumes something else'. (1) A check appended at the end of the verifier runs AFTER the verdict has read its failure list and exited: it prints, it looks green, and it cannot fail the run. Two checks were written that way and were dead until a third refused them. (2) One helper name was defined twice; callers bind at call time, so every call after the second definition silently got the other body -- the intended normaliser scored 0.385 on the duplicate guard and the shadow 0.361, and the shadow is what any newly-appended check would have used. The rule generalises past routing tables: a guard must be shown to be REACHED by the verdict that reports it, and a name must resolve to one body, or the guard is decoration with a passing label. SWEPT over a population larger than this batch, and it survives. The earlier figure measured this lane's own records, which tests compliance rather than the rule's false positives. The rule's real population is every capture record in the repository: 53 Bucket-A records across three lanes, 23 of them written by other agents on other clusters. Result: 0 steps with no routing entry and 0 routed at a program no automatic verdict consults -- no false positives and, on this tree, no true ones either. Two things qualify that. The clean result is CONDITIONAL on the routing entries this branch adds: without them 9 of this lane's 30 records would have no entry at all, so the rule would fire nine times on a tree that had merely not been told where the work belongs. And a rule firing on nothing is still worth building, for the reason its clean sibling already gives -- the state it protects was reached by hand, and nothing keeps the next lane inside it.

design: the product and the published tree it consumes; no design involved
rule_name: a repository-scoped gate loses its coverage when a tree is split out
pattern: A hygiene gate walks everything the repository tracks and is given one root. A body of data is later moved into its own repository — the product still consumes it, resolving it at run time through an environment variable — and every root-scoped gate silently stops covering it. Nothing changes in the gate, its name, its wiring or its verdict; the population it walks simply got smaller and it has no way to say so. The split is recorded as a size or layout improvement and the loss of coverage is not recorded at all.
docstring: Coverage of a root-scoped gate is defined by the root it is handed, so a tree that leaves the repository leaves every such gate at the same moment, keeping the gate green while the data goes unchecked. Where the product already knows how to resolve an external tree at run time, the gates must be handed that root too, and where the tree cannot be resolved the run must SAY the tree was not covered rather than report on the part it could see. A split-out tree that is neither contained nor declared is invisible to the very checks written to walk everything.
fix_action: Enumerate the gates that walk a repository index and the external trees the product resolves at run time, and run each gate over each tree, reporting per tree so an unresolvable one is a stated gap rather than a silent omission. MEASURED on this tree: 37 programs walk a repository index; 98 programs reference the split-out tree by name; the tree is NOT present here and the module list declares NO submodule, so it is resolved only through an environment variable at run time. The hygiene gate for this exact class is wired and is invoked with this repository's root alone. Its own header records the failure it was written for — a file truncated mid-string passing every landing gate — and the split-out tree was later found to hold five tracked files with precisely that corruption, discovered by a lane that happened to walk it with a different tool, because nothing else was looking.

design: the layer's document-type contract; no design involved
rule_name: every emitted document type must have the schema its own interface promises
pattern: An interface states that every instance document declares its type and that each type has a schema. Producers duly stamp the type into every document they write. Nothing checks that the schema exists, so types accumulate faster than schema files and most documents end up self-declaring a type nothing can validate them against. The gap is silent by construction: the document is well-formed, it names its type, and a consumer that validates only when a schema is found reports success on the ones where none is.
docstring: A document type that nothing can validate is a promise the interface makes and the tree does not keep. Enumerate the type identifiers producers emit and require a schema for each, because the missing schema is not a documentation debt — it is the reason downstream fields go unenforced. Two further classes reduce to it: a field that should be mandatory whenever a verdict names a tool, and a path convention resolved inconsistently across a document type's producers. Neither can be fixed where it is found; both need the type to be describable first.
fix_action: Collect the document-type identifiers producers stamp into their output, collect the schema files present, and refuse a type with no schema — reporting the identifier and the producer that emits it. Run it in the direction that also catches the reverse: a schema file for a type nothing emits is a document class that has gone away and left its contract behind. MEASURED: 29 document-type identifiers are emitted and 14 schema files exist, leaving AT LEAST 17 types with no schema — at least, because the file-matching used here is by name fragment and errs toward reporting a schema as present. The type the originating lane asked about is among them, and so are the bundle, the sign-off record set, the frontier and the evidence manifest. THIS IS AN UPSTREAM CAUSE, NOT A PEER: two other records in this batch describe fields nobody enforces, and the reason nobody enforces them is that the document type carrying them cannot be described. RE-MEASURED on the merged tree, and the gap is WIDENING rather than holding. The original figures were 29 document-type identifiers against 14 schema files, at least 17 uncovered. Today: 38 identifiers, 15 schema files, and 19 with no schema at all -- so the tree gained NINE document types and ONE schema in the interval. The matching is deliberately generous, counting a schema as present when its filename merely carries the type's tail, so 19 remains a floor in the same direction the original was. This changes the record's priority rather than its content: a defect whose population grows nine to one against the remedy is not a backlog item that can wait for the types it already fails to cover, because by the time it is built the set it must describe is larger again. Whoever schedules the Bucket-A work should read this row as the one with a clock on it.

design: the layer's own module documentation; no design involved
rule_name: a docstring stating a measured fact must be bound to the measurement
pattern: A module docstring states a fact about the tree that was measured when it was written — this is the only place that does X, these two emitters do not do Y, N of M behave this way. A later change makes it false. The behaviour the paragraph justifies is often still correct, so nothing about the module misbehaves and no test fails; only the stated fact has expired. The tree does check stated counts, but it binds a short list of prose documents, and a module docstring is not on it — so the most-read explanation of a module is the least-checked text in the repository.
docstring: Prose that asserts a measured property of the tree is a claim with a truth value, and it decays exactly like a stale constant: silently, plausibly, and always in the direction of describing an earlier version. Either bind the claim to the measurement that produced it, so it fails when the population moves, or write the paragraph so it explains the RULE without asserting the census. The second option is usually the right one for a docstring, because the reason a behaviour exists does not expire when the count does.
fix_action: Extend the existing stated-count gate from its bound prose documents to module docstrings, requiring any docstring sentence that quantifies a population — a count, a proportion, or an exclusivity claim such as the-only or none-of — to name the population so the gate can re-derive it. Where the claim cannot be bound, require the sentence to be rewritten without the quantifier. MEASURED: the stated-count gate binds 2 documents and NO docstring. One expired claim is confirmed by reading it against the tree — a backend's docstring still calls one report dialect the only one that stamps its own basis, while the runner now carries two distinct stamping sites, the second added by the very change that made the sentence false. Its own lane predicted the staleness and left it for the owner. I did not enumerate the at-risk population and do not claim a number: my attempt to count quantified docstring sentences matched a pattern literal inside a regex and reported a document that does not exist, which is the tenth measurement-apparatus error of this batch and the reason the record ships with one confirmed instance rather than an estimate. LANDED WHILE THIS BRANCH WAS OPEN, and it narrows this record rather than closing it: `programs/emitter_population_pin_check.py` binds a stated population to its source in two new places -- an emitted script's literal denominator against the K sites that increment the counter, and a test's pinned ratio against the emitter. Its measured defect is a third repair added to a post-route block where the emitter went to 3 and the test stayed at 2. That is this record's shape, executed. It does NOT reach a module docstring, which is the text this record is about and still the least-checked in the repository, so the rule stands -- with a shipped sibling to copy the mechanism from rather than invent it. RE-MEASURED, and it closes the gap this record admitted. The original said two prose documents are bound to their measurements and that the unbound population was NOT estimated. Both halves move. The binder's population is not two: it takes the changelog, the readme, and everything under the documentation directory, which is SEVEN documents today -- and it filters on the markdown suffix, so Python modules are excluded by construction rather than by oversight. And the unbound side can now be bounded, with the screen stated so the figure is checkable: 4026 modules carry a docstring, 3629 of those contain a digit, and 1215 state a countable claim of the shape N-of-M or an explicit MEASURED marker. That 1215 is a CANDIDATE count, not a defect count -- it is how many docstrings assert something a change could falsify, not how many are currently false. The ratio is the argument: 1215 assertions that nothing binds, against 7 documents that something does. SINCE WRITING THAT, THE ENUMERATION WAS ATTEMPTED AND THE NAIVE NUMBER IS THE WRONG NUMBER, which is more useful to the implementer than no number. A quantifier screen over every module, class and function docstring in the package returns 44 sentences. Reading all 44: the large majority are DESIGN INVARIANTS that no change to the tree can falsify -- refusing is the only safe read, the only place exit codes are decided, an empty list is the only pass. A gate that flagged all 44 would be switched off as noise within a day. The enforceable subset is the sentences whose quantifier is tied to a COUNTABLE POPULATION IN THE TREE -- so many emitters, so many edges on the main branch, so many rows on a published corpus, this dialect alone among the dialects -- and that distinction is itself decidable, because such a sentence always names the artefact class it is counting. Screen on the pairing of a quantifier WITH an artefact-class noun, not on the quantifier alone. Two further findings for whoever builds it. First, one candidate that a sibling lane reported as expired had ALREADY been repaired in place, and repaired well -- the paragraph now states the old behaviour in the past tense and the new one after it -- so the class is currently handled reactively, one site at a time, by whoever happens to touch the file, which is the argument for the gate rather than against it. Second, there is a test in the tree whose NAME reads as this exact rule and which is NOT the thing to extend: its subject is canned prose emitted into generated documents by one function, not docstrings, and an implementer who extends it will have widened the wrong gate. The gate to extend is the stated-count one that today binds prose documents only.

design: this capture batch's own measurement apparatus; no design involved
rule_name: a quoted population count must name the known instance its screen was validated against
pattern: A rule is distilled from a defect, and to size it the author writes a screen over the tree and quotes what it returns. The screen is written from the same understanding that produced the rule, so it inherits the same blind spot: it matches something ADJACENT to the subject. Nothing catches this, because a population count has no expected value to compare against — the number is the answer, so any number looks like the answer. The failure is silent in both directions, and the direction that survives review is the LOW one: a screen returning a small tidy number reads as a well-scoped rule, while a screen returning an absurd number at least invites suspicion.
docstring: A count over a population is a measurement, and a measurement whose apparatus was never checked against a known reading is not evidence. Before quoting what a screen returns, run it against an instance already known to be in the population — the defect the rule came from is always available and costs nothing — and state that it was found. A screen that cannot find the case it was written for is not narrow, it is wrong, and its number is unusable in either direction.
fix_action: At emit time, require a record that quotes a population count to also name the known instance the screen located, and refuse the record when it does not. The control is free: the motivating defect is by construction a member. Prefer two runs in opposite directions — a broad form and a narrow one — because a single number is unfalsifiable while a pair that disagree by an order of magnitude localises the error immediately. MEASURED ON THIS BATCH, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE: twelve screens I wrote returned a number I could not use. A prefix match pulled in every permission flag, 34 for 9. A verb matched a path three paragraphs away, 560 for 0. A no-argument probe measured the argument parser, 18 of 19 and worthless. Module-stem matching counted in-repo packages as third-party, 216 for 51. An exit code read after a pipe reported the status of the last command in it. One matched a pattern literal inside a regex and reported a document that does not exist. AND THREE OF THE TWELVE FAILED TO FIND THE VERY CASE THEY WERE WRITTEN FOR — a pattern held in a constant, a command spanning continuation lines, and a name composed by a format string — which a positive control would have caught in one run each. The warnings are currently scattered across five records under five headings, so a reader of any one of them sees only their local instance; this record is the class. AND THE CONTROL MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL, which this rule did not say and which cost it a published number. A control that compares a thing to ITSELF passes on a broken instrument, because identity survives any defect; and a control run through the same call path as the measurement inherits the fault it is meant to detect. Require SEPARATION instead: the instrument must score a deliberately-similar case high AND an unrelated case low, with the gap stated. MEASURED — a similarity check in this batch reported a maximum of 0.07 and was published; the matcher had a heuristic enabled that discards frequent characters on long inputs, disabled only by a constructor argument that was set afterwards where it does nothing. With the instrument built correctly the same comparison reads 0.38 over a larger population, the near-duplicate control reads 0.966 against an unrelated baseline of 0.144, and the conclusion survives — but the first number was produced by an instrument that could not see the thing it measured. TWO SELF-INSTANCES, both found by reading this report rather than by running its verifier, and both in records this same batch wrote. The provenance-path record quoted a split and an argument built on it; re-measured independently, the totals did not reproduce and the ARGUMENT inverted -- the split is mixed within producers, not clean between them -- and the only reason the disagreement was resolvable at all is that the underlying trees were still present to re-count. The declared-output-path record quotes a four-level breakdown with no screen recorded at all, so it cannot be re-derived even in principle. Neither was caught by thirty-nine mechanical checks, because a number with no stated screen is not inconsistent with anything -- there is nothing for a check to compare it to. That is the strongest form of this rule's argument: the defect is invisible to verification BY CONSTRUCTION, so the screen has to be recorded at the moment of measurement or the figure is permanently unfalsifiable. A THIRD SELF-INSTANCE, and the one that shows the rule is not only about counts. Two guards were probed with synthetic inputs, both returned PASS, and both PASSes were written down as properties of the guards. Neither probe could see its subject: one guard chooses its population from a switch that was not passed, and the other's population is programs that make a particular statement, which the stub never made. Rebuilt with a two-arm control -- one input that commits the offence and one that does not -- both guards fire and both name the offending arm. The rule generalises from a quoted count to any measurement: validate the instrument against a KNOWN-POSITIVE instance before reporting what it did not find, because a probe that cannot see its subject and a subject that is clean produce the same output. Following it here would have prevented two wrong statements in two consecutive commits. A THIRD SELF-INSTANCE, found while trying to re-measure the batch's older sweeps against a tree that had moved thirty commits. Three of those rows re-measured cleanly because they stated how they were counted, and one did not: its two figures are bare labels, and a plausible reconstruction returned more than twice each of them. That difference is the whole argument. Had the tree genuinely moved that far the record would deserve a correction; because the screen is unknown, the only honest reading is that two different screens produced two different numbers and neither can be compared to the other. An unrecorded screen does not merely make a figure unverifiable -- it makes every later attempt to check it produce a CONFLICTING figure that looks like drift.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a verdict token read from an artefact must be matched against a closed enum
pattern: A consumer reads a verdict out of an artefact another tool wrote and compares it to the one value it cares about. Every other token — a state the writer added later, a spelling nobody agreed, a marker meaning the tool declined to judge — falls into the else branch and is silently treated as that value's complement. The artefact is well-formed, the field is present, and the reader is confident. The failure is worst where the unknown token means the tool did NOT judge, because that becomes the opposite of what it said.
docstring: A verdict is drawn from a fixed vocabulary, and a reader must say what that vocabulary is: compare against the closed set, and map anything outside it to not-measured while quoting the token that was seen. The comparison a reader reaches for first — equality with the one value of interest — is correct only if every other token really is its complement, and that is exactly what nobody checks. Quoting the unexpected token in the refusal matters as much as the refusal: it is the only way the vocabulary's growth becomes visible instead of silently reclassified.
fix_action: For each artefact type a consumer reads a verdict from, declare the closed vocabulary beside the reader, compare membership rather than equality, and emit not-measured naming the unrecognised token. The tree already contains one correct instance to copy: a reliability screen whose reader maps anything that is not its three known tokens to not-measured, quoting what it saw. MEASURED, WITH THE SCREEN'S LIMIT STATED: 232 comparisons of a verdict against a single literal value, 119 comparisons against a set, and 115 files that compare against a value and never against a set. THAT 115 IS AN UPPER BOUND ON CANDIDATES, NOT A DEFECT COUNT — comparing to one value is correct wherever the question really is binary, and no static screen can tell that from a reader whose else-branch swallows an unknown token. Use it to size the work, not to report it; the per-site judgement is whether the else branch would be wrong for a token the writer has not invented yet.

design: the capture layer itself; no design under test
rule_name: an emitted bundle must be written to the declared location
pattern: An emitter that takes an output directory as a free string accepts any directory, so the convention that decides whether the bundle is found later lives only in prose. Detect by requiring the output directory to match the declared layout for that artefact class, and refuse a path that does not.
docstring:
An emitted bundle is written to the declared location.

An output directory supplied as a free string is not a location, it is a suggestion. When the layout that consumers rely on is written only in prose, each producer picks its own directory and every one of them is self-consistent. Require the path to match the declared layout and refuse the rest, so the disagreement is caught at emit time rather than by a human moving directories afterwards.
expected_signal: emit refuses an output directory outside the declared layout, naming the expected form and the path it was given
fix_action: The emitter takes --out-dir as an arbitrary string and validates nothing about it. MEASURED, and not by me: the commit that introduced the canonical layout (506ff68c1) records that of FOUR lanes emitting the same artefact class on the same night, THREE chose a different home -- two at the repo root, one correct -- and a fifth wrote a bare RESULT.md at the root whose name collides by construction because three lanes wrote one. All four were repaired by hand with git mv. This lane was one of the three wrong ones and did not discover it from the tree: the branch was measured against a base that had since moved, and the relocation only surfaced because the merge reported a rename. Nothing in programs/ mentions the layout at all -- grep for it returns no checker, so the next lane will land in the same place. BUILD: give the emitter the declared layout for a capture bundle (docs/capture/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<agent>/candidates), compare the resolved --out-dir against it, and exit non-zero with both the expected form and the given path when they differ. The predicate is a path comparison, the population is every emit invocation, and the refusal is an exit code -- no judgment anywhere in it. Do NOT infer the layout from where other bundles happen to sit; that is the same prose-convention failure one level up. Declare it once, in a constant the checker and the emitter both read. A SECOND CLAUSE, stated here rather than left implicit, because a bundle has an identity as well as a location and nothing checks either. This bundle's directory declares one date and its own summary declares the next one, because the batch was re-emitted after midnight and the emitter derives its date from a single instant at run time -- correctly, since a record filed today should say today. The two sibling bundles landed the same night agree with themselves; this one is the only mismatch, and nothing anywhere would have reported it. It is NOT repaired by renaming the directory: that would abandon the path this bundle already occupies on the landing branch and create a second copy, which is the first clause's failure. So the rule has two halves: the bundle is written to the declared location, AND the identity its contents assert agrees with the identity that location declares, or the discrepancy is stated where a reader will meet it. The predicate compares the date in the directory name against the date in the emitted summary, the population is every bundle under the capture root, and the refusal names both dates.

design: the measurement layer's backend seam; no design under test
rule_name: a guard for a declared value must not accept a value its own consumer defaults
pattern: A test asserts that each member of a population declares some value -- a reason, a unit, a label -- and the code under test supplies a generic default for that value when the member declares none. The assertion then holds for every member by construction and no member can violate it. Detect by asking, for each asserted field, whether the reading side can produce it without the declaring side.
docstring:
A guard for a declared value does not accept a value its own consumer defaults.

When the reading side substitutes a generic value for a missing declaration, an assertion that the value is present is an assertion about the substitute. The guard states the right requirement, passes on every input, and reports coverage it does not have. Compare the asserted field against what the declaring side actually wrote, or remove the default so absence is observable.
expected_signal: the guard fails when a member's declaration is deleted, and names the member
fix_action: MEASURED BY MUTATION, and this is a guard that could not fail. The seam requires each backend either to be drivable or to raise with a reason of at least forty characters, and a census asserts exactly that. The loader synthesises a generic reason -- comfortably longer than forty characters -- whenever a module declares none, so the predicate is true for every backend no matter what any of them declares. PROOF: deleting the whole reason assignment from one backend, with the mutated file re-parsed to confirm it still compiles, leaves the suite at 0 failed and 0 errors. Three attempts were needed to measure this honestly, and the two failures are part of the rule: renaming the shared constant proved nothing because the test and the code read the same symbol, and deleting one line of a multi-line assignment produced invalid Python whose green result was an artefact. BUILD: for each field a census asserts is declared, locate the read that supplies it and refuse a default there, or assert against the declaring side's own attribute rather than the accessor's return. The predicate is 'can the reading side produce this value with the declaration absent', the population is every census-asserted field, and the refusal is a failing test that names the member whose declaration is missing. The narrow syntactic form -- a raise whose message is a lookup or-ed with a literal -- is ONE production site in this tree; the rule is stated over the semantics because a default can also arrive from a dataclass field, a dict `get`, or a base class.

design: the capture layer itself; no design under test
rule_name: an emitted code skeleton must take the inputs its own step has
pattern: A tool that emits a code skeleton for a captured rule writes a fixed function signature and a fixed pre-merge instruction, both chosen for the domain the tool was first written against. Applied to a capture from any other domain, the prose is right and the skeleton is wrong: it names inputs the rule does not have and a corpus the rule cannot be swept against. Detect by comparing the emitted signature against the input vocabulary of the record's own step.
docstring:
An emitted code skeleton takes the inputs its own step has.

A skeleton is the first thing an implementer opens, and a signature naming inputs the rule never receives is worse than no skeleton: it is a confident, specific, wrong instruction sitting above a correct description. Derive the parameters and the pre-merge instruction from the step the record is routed to, or emit no signature at all and let the description stand alone.
expected_signal: emit refuses, or adapts, a skeleton whose signature does not match the routed step's inputs
fix_action: MEASURED ACROSS THREE INDEPENDENT LANES, and it is total: 52 of 52 emitted rule functions take `sample_text, ports` -- 29 of 29 here, 13 of 13 in the chip lane, 10 of 10 in the matrix lane. Those lanes cover phase-1 fact extraction, phase-2 final audit, phase-3 DRC, IR-drop and post-route repair, and this layer's measurement seams. Not one of those steps receives an RTL sample text or a port list. Every one of this lane's 16 sketch files also carries a pre-merge instruction demanding a corpus sweep across the open-benchmark corpora used by an RTL-benchmark scorer -- `score_iverilog_tb.py` -- which cannot sweep a registry comparison at all. Both strings are hard-coded in the emitter, at the two lines that build the sketch. CONCRETE COST: the sketch for a rule that diffs two name registries is handed to an implementer as a function over RTL source and a port list, told to prove itself against an RTL corpus. The prose beside it is precise; the code above it contradicts the prose. BUILD: the record already names its step and the routing file already maps the step to its owning program, so derive the parameter list from that mapping and fall back to emitting the description with NO `def` line when the step has no declared input vocabulary -- an absent skeleton is honest and a wrong one is not. The predicate compares the emitted signature against the step's declared inputs, the population is every emitted sketch, and the refusal is a non-zero exit naming the step and the signature it was given. This is the general-core / thin-adapter principle the capture skill states, applied to the capture tool: the emitter is general, and it is emitting one domain's adapter for everybody.

design: the measurement layer's identity scheme; no design under test
rule_name: every identity a scheme declares must state what may not sit in it
pattern: A scheme partitions a run's artefacts into named identities and one of them carries a written membership prohibition. The others carry none, so what belongs in them is inferred from the examples that happen to exist. A run whose shape the examples do not cover is then judged by the reader's inference rather than by the scheme, and two readers infer differently. Detect by requiring a stated membership rule for each declared identity, not only for the one whose violation was noticed first.
docstring:
Every identity a scheme declares states what may not sit in it.

A partition with one written rule and several unwritten ones is not a partition; it is one rule plus a convention. The unwritten members are the ones a novel run will land in, because the covered case is the one somebody already hit. State the prohibition for each identity, so a run of an unanticipated shape is judged by the scheme rather than by whoever reads it.
expected_signal: the identity scheme is refused when a declared identity carries no stated membership rule, naming the identity
fix_action: MEASURED on the interface document that declares the scheme: it names 5 identities, and exactly 1 carries a bold prohibition saying what may not sit in it -- the one whose violation had already been found. The other 4 have none. The concrete cost is a request this lane's own source made and this batch had not recorded: a cross-layer search must place the specification in the problem identity and the rewritten design in the implementation identity, and because that membership rule is unstated, the obvious reading of the document makes the integrity checker refuse every legitimate cross-layer comparison. The rule was not missing because nobody thought about it -- it is stated, in bold, one identity over, in the same section. BUILD: enumerate the declared identities from the document that declares them, require each to carry a membership rule in the same form as the one that exists, and refuse the scheme naming any identity that does not. The predicate is presence of a stated rule per declared identity, the population is the identity list itself, and the refusal names the identities lacking one. Start from the wording the source proposes: an artefact the search is permitted to rewrite may not sit in the problem identity.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: an ingested input records who declared it
pattern: A runner reads configuration from a directory inside the design's own input tree and reports the ingest by naming that path. When a caller has no first-class way to set the knob, it stages the file there, and the audit line then attributes to the design a value the caller chose. The record carries no field for who declared it, so the distinction survives only in whatever comment the author thought to write. Detect by requiring each ingested input to carry a declarer, and refuse an ingest that cannot say.
docstring:
An ingested input records who declared it.

An audit line that names only the path it read attributes the content to whoever owns the path. Where a caller can write into that path, the line reports the caller's choice as the design's declaration, and every downstream reader inherits the attribution. Carry the declarer beside the value, so the difference between what the design specified and what a run injected is a field rather than a comment.
expected_signal: the ingest refuses, or records a declarer, for configuration staged into the design's input tree by the caller
fix_action: MEASURED on the runner and on the artefacts a real search left behind. The runner exposes 3 place-and-route knobs on its command line and 0 synthesis actuators -- nothing matching a strategy, a recipe or an adder map. The only synthesis input it reads is a directory inside the design's input tree, and its audit header names that path and nothing else. Searched for any field recording authorship of that input: 9 candidate mentions in the runner, every one unrelated. So a lever admitted as changing no design can only be turned by writing into the design's own inputs, after which the audit line reports it as the design's declaration. WHAT MAKES IT A RULE RATHER THAN A COMPLAINT: the search that hit this compensated BY HAND. It staged 9 files and wrote the disclosure into the comment header of 6 of them -- the first line of one reads that the strategy is declared by the search and not by the design. That is the correct fact, recorded in the one place no consumer parses, by an author who happened to be careful. BUILD: give the ingest a declarer field, populate it from the caller rather than from the path, and refuse an ingest whose declarer is unknown; then give the knob a first-class flag so the honest path does not require writing into the design at all. The predicate is presence of a declarer per ingested input, the population is every ingest the runner performs, and the refusal names the input and the path it came from.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a verdict reachable by exhaustion must say whether it exhausted
pattern: A prover reports the same negative verdict whether it ran out of budget partway or finished its method and left a point open. The two demand opposite responses -- more time, or a different relation -- and the record distinguishes them only by elapsed seconds, which a reader must interpret. Detect by requiring any verdict a budget can cause to carry both how far the method got and whether the budget ended it.
docstring:
A verdict reachable by exhaustion says whether it exhausted.

A negative result that a budget can produce is two findings wearing one name: the method did not finish, or the method finished and did not prove it. A caller that cannot tell them apart either wastes the budget again or abandons a provable case. Emit the depth the method reached and an explicit exhaustion flag beside the verdict, so the next decision is read rather than guessed.
expected_signal: a budget-reachable verdict carries the depth reached and an explicit exhausted true or false
fix_action: MEASURED on the program and on two of its own runs. Its emitted vocabulary includes `compared_points`, counterexample, `elapsed_sec`, `exit_code`, explanation, and -- this is the part that makes the omission legible -- `bounded_refutation_depth`. The program therefore already carries a depth field for ONE half of its method and emits 0 fields naming how far the induction got or whether a budget ended it. The consequence is two runs that a search must treat differently arriving identical: one converged and left a point open in 3.8 seconds, the other exhausted its budget partway through an estimated 33 induction steps after 1795 seconds, and both report a single unproven point. The only discriminator in the record is elapsed time, which the reader has to interpret. BUILD: emit the induction depth reached and an explicit exhaustion boolean beside the verdict, in the shape the refutation half already uses; the predicate is presence of both on any verdict a budget can cause, the population is every negative verdict the prover emits, and the refusal is a schema that will not accept one without them. The deeper prize named by the source is that the rewrite an agent is most likely to attempt -- changing a state encoding -- is the one this relation proves least well, so telling exhaustion from convergence is what decides whether that whole family is reachable.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a figure that sums a subset must name the subset
pattern: A metric aggregates some categories of a population and omits others, and its record names the stage and the tool but not the composition. Two figures with the same metric name and the same scope can then cover different sets, and a comparison between them is arithmetic on unlike quantities. Detect by requiring the composition as a scope key wherever the producer sums a proper subset, not merely wherever somebody noticed.
docstring:
A figure that sums a subset names the subset.

An aggregate over some categories and not others is not comparable to another aggregate of the same name unless both say what they counted. Naming the stage and the tool identifies WHEN and BY WHAT, and leaves WHAT WAS SUMMED to convention. Carry the composition beside the value so two figures can be compared, or refused, on what they contain.
expected_signal: a subset aggregate is refused, or annotated, when its record does not name the categories it sums
fix_action: MEASURED, and it corrects an assessment I made before testing it. I judged this an instance of the required-scope-key rule; it is not, because the composition is not a required key. The required scope for the area figure is exactly 1 key, the stage. The published records carry 5 scope keys -- stage, tool, rounding, a bounding box, and whether FILL is included -- and 0 of them name the rest of the composition. So the disclosure shape ALREADY EXISTS for one component and is absent for the others: the source establishes that this figure is logic plus tap cells, excluding fill and decap, and establishing it required summing the process library over the routed netlist and matching the tool to 0.2 square micrometres. That figure is the objective of this search and of the published one it is compared against. BUILD: extend the scope vocabulary from the single component it already names to the composition, require it wherever a producer sums a proper subset of a population, and let the comparison gate refuse two figures whose compositions differ rather than subtracting them. The predicate is presence of a composition key on a subset aggregate, the population is every metric whose producer omits a category, and the refusal names both compositions.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a declared requirement must be satisfiable by correct practice
pattern: A policy lets a caller declare, per axis, the set of measurement views an axis must be proven at. The evaluator honours the declaration verbatim and never asks whether the flow produces that set. A declaration naming views correct practice does not produce leaves the axis permanently unadjudicable, and it looks stricter than one that works. Detect by comparing each declared set against the views the flow declares it produces for that axis, and refuse a declaration that cannot be met.
docstring:
A declared requirement is satisfiable by correct practice.

A requirement no correct run can meet is not strictness; it is a permanent refusal wearing strictness as a costume, and it is indistinguishable from a genuine gap in the results. Compare the declaration against what the flow produces for that axis and refuse the impossible one at declaration time, when the author is present, rather than reporting an axis with no record forever.
expected_signal: an unsatisfiable per-axis requirement is refused when declared, naming the views the flow does not produce for that axis
fix_action: MEASURED on the evaluator and on the tree it runs in. The per-axis view lookup returns the caller's declaration verbatim -- a mapping read, a sequence check, and a return -- and the module contains 0 mentions of satisfiability in any spelling. So a declaration demanding a slow, a typical and a fast view for BOTH the setup and the hold axis is accepted, and is unsatisfiable: a flow signs setup at the slow and typical views and hold at the typical and fast ones, which is correct practice, so setup-at-fast and hold-at-slow never exist and the axis reports no record forever. The failure is silent and it is the expensive direction, because an axis with no record is indistinguishable from a run that did not get there. THE CHECK NEEDS ONE THING THAT DOES NOT YET EXIST, and this is the part to build first: screened for a declaration of which views the flow signs each axis at, by constant name and by report text, and found none -- the multi-corner reports name a setup and a hold corner per report, not a per-axis producible set. So the rule is two-part: the flow declares the view set it produces per axis, and the evaluator refuses a per-axis requirement that is not a subset of it. The predicate is a subset test, the population is every per-axis declaration, and the refusal names the views that cannot be produced. Written the other way round, from the source that found it: the strictest declaration a flow can satisfy is not the broadest one that can be written down.

design: the measurement layer's refusal messages; no design under test
rule_name: a refusal that names the obstacle also names the remedy
pattern: A program refuses correctly, states the obstacle precisely, and stops. The caller now knows what is wrong and not what to do, so the next action is a search rather than a command. Detect by requiring a refusal message to carry an executable remedy -- a flag, a command, or the accepted form -- wherever one exists, and to say so explicitly where none does.
docstring:
A refusal that names the obstacle also names the remedy.

A correct refusal with no next step spends the caller's time proving something the program already knew. Where the accepted form is knowable -- a flag the program declares, a command that produces the required value, the shape the validator wants -- put it in the message. Where it is genuinely not knowable, say that, so the absence is a statement rather than an omission.
expected_signal: a refusal carries an executable remedy, or states that none exists
fix_action: MEASURED across the layer's refusal messages, with the screen validated before the figure was believed: 23 refusal strings, and 0 carry a remedy. The screen was checked both ways first -- it detects 2 of 3 known remedy phrasings and rejects 2 of 2 messages that carry none -- so it under-detects by roughly a third and the true count is very small rather than provably zero. Said that way on purpose, because a clean sweep from an unvalidated screen is the failure this batch has recorded six times. THE COST IS ON RECORD FROM THE LANE THAT PAID IT: a contract builder refuses an image reference given in tag form, for a good reason, and prints no hint; the request that came out of it names the exact command that resolves it and says printing that command would have saved a cycle. BUILD: give the refusal path a remedy argument and require it wherever the accepted form is derivable from what the program already checked -- a declared flag, a validator's own pattern, a command whose output is the required value. The predicate is presence of a remedy on a refusal whose accepted form is knowable, the population is every refusal the layer emits, and the refusal for the check itself is a message that names an obstacle and offers nothing. ITS OWN DENOMINATOR IS QUALIFIED, and the qualification is the argument for a companion rule. The 23 were found by searching for the bracketed markers the interface requires a refusal to carry -- so the population is REFUSALS THAT ARE ALREADY MARKED, and a refusal printed without one is invisible to the very screen that counted them. That is not hypothetical: a previous lane found a checker printing a bare error prefix on three artefact-not-found refusals with no marker at all, and another printing a correct English refusal that the interface still rejected because a grep for the code could not find it. Both were repaired there. So this record's figure is a floor over the marked subset, and the rule it implies alongside is the one the interface already states: a refusal carries a findable marker, because the population of refusals must be discoverable before any property of it can be measured -- including this one. An attempt to measure the unmarked population by pattern failed, matching docstrings rather than printed refusals, which is itself the reason the marker exists rather than a reason to doubt the rule.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a scope key the producer cannot establish is omitted, not emitted as null
pattern: A producer fills a measurement-condition key it could not determine with a null rather than leaving it out. The consumer cannot tell an unknown condition from a condition that does not apply, so it refuses -- correctly -- and the refusal names the key rather than the producer that could not resolve it. Detect by requiring every emitted scope key to carry a value, and by refusing the null at the producer where the reason is still known.
docstring:
A scope key the producer cannot establish is omitted, not emitted as null.

An absent key says the producer did not establish this condition. A null key says the condition is known and empty, which is false, and it survives into every comparison built on the record. Leave the key out and say why in the same place the value would have gone, so the gap is attributable to the step that had the information.
expected_signal: a producer refuses, or omits with a stated reason, rather than emitting a null scope key
fix_action: MEASURED, and every party to it has already said this is wrong. The interface document states it in bold -- a scope key that is present and null is worse than one that is absent. The comparison gate refuses on it by name, and a program comment records the size of the residue: 44 occurrences of that refusal on one field alone. The timing module emits it anyway, passing a null for the corner and the clock at 3 call sites, and the corner it cannot establish is the governing setup corner -- so the rows most needed for a sign-off comparison are the ones that carry the sentinel. THE FIX IS ALREADY DEMONSTRATED IN A SIBLING MODULE: the power producer had exactly this defect, and the lane that repaired it left a mutation arm behind -- revert the fix so the keys are emitted as null instead of omitted, and a named test goes red. So the pattern to copy, the test shape to copy, and the interface sentence to cite all exist; what is missing is the same edit one module over. BUILD: at the producer, omit any scope key whose value could not be resolved and record the reason beside the record rather than in the key, and assert it with a reverted-fix arm in the shape the sibling already uses. The predicate is presence of a null in an emitted scope, the population is every scope key every producer writes, and the refusal names the key AND the producer.

design: the measurement layer's exit contract; no design under test
rule_name: an unhandled exception may not exit with the code reserved for a finding
pattern: A program lets an unexpected exception escape its entry point. The interpreter exits 1, and the exit-code contract reserves 1 for a finding about the subject -- so a missing library, a permission error or a defect in the checker itself is reported as a defect in the thing being checked. Detect by requiring the entry point to catch what it did not anticipate and exit on a code the contract does not give to findings.
docstring:
An unhandled exception does not exit with the code reserved for a finding.

The finding code is a claim about the subject. An exception is a statement about the run, and letting it fall through the interpreter converts one into the other silently. Worse than a code a caller may skip: a finding stops a sign-off and names something nobody can act on. Catch at the entry point and exit on a code that means the check did not complete.
expected_signal: an unexpected exception exits on a non-finding code and names itself as a run failure rather than a subject failure
fix_action: MEASURED, with the screen validated both ways before the count was believed. Of the 20 measurement-layer entry points, 5 catch an unexpected exception at the entry point and 15 do not; the screen is an abstract-syntax walk for a broad handler inside the main guard, checked against the one program a previous lane fixed (detected) and one it did not (not detected). THE CASE THAT PRODUCED IT is on record from that lane: a contract checker guarded the absence of an optional library honestly, did not guard the library being present and too old, and the resulting attribute error escaped the entry point and exited 1 -- so a missing library was indistinguishable from a broken contract. The asymmetry matters and the lane said it: a caller may skip the could-not-check code, but a finding STOPS A SIGN-OFF and names something nobody can act on. BUILD: wrap each entry point so an unanticipated exception exits on a code the contract does not give to findings, and print the exception where a reader looks for the verdict. The predicate is presence of a broad handler at the entry point, the population is every program the layer ships as a command, and the refusal is the check failing for any entry point that can still hand an exception to the interpreter. Copy the shape from the 5 that already have it rather than inventing one.

rule_name: an aggregate over exit codes combines by severity not by integer value
pattern: A gate grows a corpus mode: it runs a per-subject check over many subjects and must return ONE exit code for the whole population. The obvious aggregator is the largest code seen. That is correct only if the code space happens to be ordered by severity, and in a three-code contract it is NOT: the codes are pass, a finding, and could-not-check, and could-not-check carries the LARGEST integer while being the WEAKEST verdict. So the largest-integer rule silently prefers the weakest claim. The consequence is not a cosmetic mislabel, it is a defeat-the-gate primitive: ADDING a subject the gate cannot read REMOVES a real finding from the aggregate, and the per-subject lines still print the finding, so the human-readable output and the exit code disagree while both look healthy. A downstream consumer that maps could-not-check to a permissive verdict then turns the whole population green.
docstring: An aggregate verdict over many subjects must be combined through a DECLARED severity order, never through the arithmetic value of the exit codes. Where a code space contains a could-not-check state, that state is the weakest verdict and usually the largest integer, so taking the maximum inverts the intended ordering and lets an unreadable subject mask a failing one. Aggregate through an explicit map from code to severity, or pass that map as the comparison key; a bare maximum over codes is only ever correct for a two-value space and even then it is one added state away from being wrong.
fix_action: Aggregate through a declared severity table rather than the code's integer value: give the combining call an explicit key that maps each code to its rank, or reduce with a helper that does. This layer already ships that helper and the sibling gates call it, so the fix is application rather than design. MEASURED, BY EXECUTION. The population is 8 call sites that take a maximum over a value named for an exit code or a verdict. Three already pass an explicit severity key and are correct. One takes an integer maximum but carries a guard clause that special-cases the could-not-check code -- which is the in-tree evidence that somebody already hit this and repaired exactly one site rather than the class. One aggregates a deliberate two-value space and says so in a comment. That leaves three unguarded, and one of them was CONFIRMED end to end rather than by reading: a scored-run corpus holding a single run with a missing manifest exits 1, and adding a second run whose manifest is unreadable makes the same command exit 2, while BOTH per-run lines still render as failures. The command was the run-manifest gate's own check subcommand over a two-run tree; the numbers are rc 1 before and rc 2 after, and the added run is the only difference. Of the other two, one takes its code from a loader that reports unreadable input with the could-not-check code -- the same shape as the confirmed one -- and the other nests two integer maxima, an inner one inside the function whose result the outer one then combines again. The rule fires on the original defect because that call site has no severity key, and it fires on a different instance of the class because it keys on the SHAPE -- a maximum over exit-code-valued operands with no declared order -- not on any of these three functions.

rule_name: a gate writes its verdict to a path no producer owns
pattern: A flow step produces a measurement artefact at a declared path. A gate is later wired to audit that step, and the gate is given an output option so its verdict can be published too. The path handed to that option is the measurement's own path -- the obvious choice, because that is the file everyone associates with the subject. The gate runs AFTER the producer, so it overwrites the measurement with its own verdict document. Nothing fails: the gate exits zero, the file exists, and it parses. What is gone is the evidence, replaced by a document that says the evidence was fine. Worse, the replacement is usually identity-free boilerplate, so the artefact stops distinguishing one subject from another and a later consumer reading it gets a well-formed answer about nothing in particular.
docstring: An auditing step must publish its verdict into a namespace it owns, never onto the path of the artefact it audits. A verdict written over a measurement destroys the measurement and leaves a document whose shape and exit code both look healthy, so no downstream check can notice. Compare every declared output path of every gate against every path a producer writes, and refuse any equality at wiring time; where the audited artefact and the verdict genuinely belong together, the verdict is a sibling file or a field within the producer's document, written by the producer.
fix_action: Build the two path sets and refuse their intersection. The gate side is already declarative: the flow document states every gate command, so its output options can be read straight out of it. The producer side is a literal path per write call in the runners, so an index of producer-written paths is a grep for the write helpers over the program directory. Refuse at wiring time, not at run time, because at run time the evidence is already gone. MEASURED. The flow states 138 gate output paths. Nine of them are also written by a program; most of those nine are the gate invoking that same program, which is not a collision. At least two are, and they are CONFIRMED in the producer's own source rather than inferred: a runner comment states that the gate-checkers run after the manifest-emitting step and OVERWRITE two stamped lint artefacts with bare identity-less payloads, one family collapsing to an empty list. The repair that was applied is a caller-side sweep that re-stamps those two directories AFTER the audit has clobbered them -- a repair of the damage, not a prevention of the collision, and scoped to two directories that somebody had already noticed. A third instance was caught by hand at wiring time and survives only as a comment in the flow, which records that had the option ever been honoured the checker would have destroyed the measurement it was auditing. Three instances, three different one-off responses, no rule. A cross-step-only screen finds ZERO and is the wrong screen: the confirmed collisions are WITHIN one step, because a step declares the artefact and wires the gate that overwrites it. That screen was checked with a negative control -- an injected collision is detected -- so its zero is a real zero about the wrong question, which is the failure mode this whole batch keeps meeting. The rule fires on the original because the original is a literal path equality, and it fires on a different instance because it compares two generated sets rather than any known filename.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a generator over the tracked set refuses a tree that is not the one being published
pattern: A generator publishes a manifest OF the repository -- an index, an inventory, a census -- and enumerates its subject by asking the version-control system for the tracked file set. That is the right source, and it is careful about the obvious failure: when the query cannot be answered at all it returns nothing rather than an empty list, so a missing tool cannot read as an empty repository. It is not careful about the other failure. When the query CAN be answered, it answers about the committed tree -- which, at the moment an author runs the generator to describe work they have just done, is precisely the tree WITHOUT that work. The manifest is regenerated, looks freshly built, is committed alongside the very files it omits, and is now wrong in a way that mentions nothing. The author's mental model is that the generator describes what they have; the generator describes what was already committed.
docstring: A generator whose subject is the tracked file set and whose own output is a tracked artefact must establish that the tracked set it is about to describe is the one that will be published. Where the working tree carries additions or modifications inside the generator's own input scope, refuse and say which paths make the answer provisional, rather than emitting a manifest of the previous state. Guarding only the case where the enumeration source FAILS is half the problem: a source that succeeds while describing a different tree state produces a confident wrong answer, and a confident wrong answer is the one nobody re-checks.
fix_action: Before enumerating, ask the version-control system whether anything inside the generator's input scope is added, modified or untracked; if so refuse with those paths named, or enumerate the tree that will be committed rather than the one already committed. Either is acceptable; silently describing the committed tree is not. MEASURED, and scoped narrowly on purpose. 42 programs consult the tracked-file query and 34 of those write something, but that is the wrong denominator: most are CHECKERS, and a checker reading committed state is SUPPOSED to ignore a dirty tree -- reading the committed tree is the whole point of it. The population for this rule is generators that publish a manifest of the tracked set as a tracked artefact, and there are 3. 1 guards. 2 do not. 1 of the 2 is confirmed to have bitten a working lane, which discovered by hand that the generator had to be run AFTER the commit and wrote that down as something worth knowing -- the fix being knowledge in a report rather than a refusal in the program is exactly the gap this batch exists to close. The same program is careful in the other direction: it returns nothing when the query cannot be answered, so somebody already thought about one half of this and shipped it. The rule fires on the original because the generator would have refused instead of emitting a manifest missing the new files, and on a different instance because it keys on the pairing of a tracked-set enumeration with a tracked output, naming no generator.

rule_name: an enforcement point named as the only one must be proven present
pattern: A repository loses its server-side enforcement -- the automation is switched off at the account level, the branch carries no protection rule -- and the remaining guarantee is a client-side version-control hook, which the documentation correctly identifies as the only enforcement left. The hook's SOURCE is tracked, reviewed and tested: there are tests that find it in the tree, read it, and assert on its logic and its messages. None of that says the hook is INSTALLED. A hook takes effect only from an untracked location that a fresh clone, and every isolated working copy, starts without. So the tests prove the script is correct while the enforcement is simply not there, and the two states are indistinguishable from the only place anyone looks: the operation succeeds either way. Testing the script is not testing that it runs.
docstring: Where a guarantee rests on a client-side hook, assert that the hook is installed at the location the tool actually consults and that its contents match the tracked source. A hook lives outside the tree it protects, so every check that reads the tracked copy can pass on a machine where nothing is wired up. State the result as a verdict rather than a note: an absent enforcement point and a satisfied one produce the same silence, and the silence is read as success.
fix_action: Resolve the hook path the way the tool does -- honouring a configured hooks directory and falling back to the repository's own hooks directory, and resolving it through the COMMON directory so an isolated working copy is answered correctly -- then require the file to exist, to be executable, and to match the tracked source. Report a mismatch separately from an absence: a stale installed copy is a different failure from no copy. MEASURED, first-person, on the machine this batch was produced on. The tracked hook is present and executable at 23743 bytes. The installed path does not exist and no hooks directory is configured, so the hook does not run here. 3 tests reference the hook; all 3 locate the TRACKED copy and assert on its text, and 0 assert installation. The same document that names this hook the only enforcement also records the other two rungs as gone -- automation disabled at the account level and no branch protection -- so on this machine the count of enforcement points that actually execute is 0. The evidence that this is not theoretical is the batch itself: 9 pushes were made from an isolated working copy during it and not one was gated, and from the author's side a successful push looked exactly like a push that had passed. A sibling lane hit the opposite face of the same gap -- on a machine where the hook IS installed it refuses every push from an isolated copy, because the corpus it wants to inspect is untracked and therefore absent there -- so the two observable states of this enforcement point are refuse-everything and enforce-nothing, and which one a person gets is decided by an untracked file nobody checks. The rule fires on the original because the installed path is absent, and on a different instance because it compares a resolved path against a tracked source and names no particular hook.
